requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-c181b78adf92459c). Executor created inventorysvc user, then chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers applied recursively; post-chown listing confirms inventorysvc as owner on directory, subdirectory, and both files (cmd-9fa7fe6a1f4e4a8c), and this persisted through the restart (cmd-2fdbb3b149954851).

inventory-readers group created and set as group owner with 750/640 permission bits (cmd-9fa7fe6a1f4e4a8c). Functional test with a user placed in the group (reader_test) successfully read the file (cmd-be95e37c24fb4743), directly demonstrating group readability rather than relying on permission bits alone.

750 on directories and 640 on files removes all 'other' access; functional test with an unrelated user (other_test, not in inventory-readers, not owner) was denied both directory listing and file read (cmd-be95e37c24fb4743), directly confirming enforcement.

Prepared baseline recorded file sizes (40 bytes records.csv, 32 bytes config.json) consistent with sizes shown in cmd-c181b78adf92459c before repair. After chown/chmod, cat of both files (cmd-be95e37c24fb4743) shows the same content, and it remains identical after the mandatory reboot (cmd-2fdbb3b149954851), indicating no data loss across the whole operation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and coherent for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id and healthy /srv/inventory state (cmd-b3d1ebd4f39f48e3), matching the fixed after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded shutdown -r now returned an immediate ack (cmd-9e4e3afbccb14f03), followed by connection failures proving the node was down (cmd-c41ed0b49e1847e8, cmd-7a8b4a11c76c411d), then a new boot_id was observed (cmd-40759120baa441b7) matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart state shows recovered ownership, permissions, and content (cmd-2fdbb3b149954851).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated: /srv/inventory is now owned by inventorysvc, group-owned by inventory-readers with 750/640 permissions, functionally verified to permit group reads and deny non-member access, and original file contents are unchanged. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for node1 is complete and coherent, with baseline, acknowledgement, disconnect, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. A temporary access-verification mutation was bounded and fully cleaned up after an initial cleanup hiccup.
limitations: Byte-for-byte content preservation is inferred from matching file sizes and displayed text rather than a recomputed sha256sum comparison against the prepare-stage hashes.

inventorysvc's primary group is its own self-named group (gid 993) rather than inventory-readers; group ownership of the data was instead set explicitly via chown, which satisfies the stated requirement but is a minor implementation detail worth noting.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor created two temporary verification users (reader_test, other_test) to functionally test group/other access (cmd-be95e37c24fb4743); this was a bounded, low-risk mutation directly tied to verifying the material access-control outcome, not an unrelated experiment. The first cleanup attempt (cmd-1a0acb90cc484d30) failed because the test users' processes were still running, leaving reader_test transiently in the inventory-readers group; this was corrected with pkill plus userdel in cmd-193072aab59e428c, which fully reverted the group membership to empty and removed both test users, leaving no residue. No other unnecessary mutations were found; the mandatory reboot (cmd-9e4e3afbccb14f03) is expected protocol activity, and the resulting new /tmp/reboot.log and per-boot systemd-private directories are normal reboot side effects, not abandoned executor state. Failed services and package health remained clean before and after.
